seoTitle: Free Security Headers Generator: HSTS, CSP, X-Frame
metaDescription: Generate HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options and related security headers for Apache, NGINX, Netlify or Cloudflare. Free; in your browser.
intro: Choose a platform and values for CSP, HSTS and X-Frame-Options to generate security header configuration for Apache, NGINX, Netlify _headers or a Cloudflare Worker.
why:
Security headers are cheap protection against clickjacking, content sniffing and downgrade attacks, but their syntax differs between servers, and a wrong HSTS or CSP setting can lock visitors out or break the page.

This generator produces a set of headers in the format for Apache, NGINX, Netlify or a Cloudflare Worker. You enter your Content-Security-Policy, the HSTS max-age, whether to include preload, and the X-Frame-Options value. The output includes a reminder to test CSP in Report-Only mode first, and a warning about HSTS preload, which is difficult to undo. Check the result with the headers analyzer after deployment. Generation happens in your browser, and nothing is sent to a server.
howTo: Choose your platform: Apache, NGINX, Netlify or Cloudflare.
Enter your Content-Security-Policy and the HSTS max-age, and decide on preload.
Choose SAMEORIGIN or DENY for X-Frame-Options.
Run the tool, add the configuration to your server and test with the headers analyzer.

faq.q: Is HSTS preload safe to enable?
faq.a: Only when every subdomain supports HTTPS permanently. Preloading puts your domain in browser lists and removal is slow, so read the preload requirements first and start with a short max-age.

faq.q: Should I start with a strict CSP?
faq.a: Start with Report-Only to see what would be blocked. A CSP that is too strict breaks inline scripts and third-party widgets, so tune it before enforcing.
CSP frame-ancestors is the modern way, but X-Frame-Options is still honoured by older browsers, so many sites send both.
